```artifact
Feature: Alarms
  As a user
  I want the GUI to compute and display alarms correctly
  So that I can be notified of potential issues

  Scenario: HIGH VTE alarm computation
    Given the current breath VTE is above the threshold
    When the GUI computes the alarm
    Then the HIGH VTE alarm is active

  Scenario: LOW VTE alarm priority
    Given the current breath VTE is below the threshold
    When the GUI computes the alarm
    Then the LOW VTE alarm has medium priority

  Scenario: HIGH VTE alarm priority
    Given the current breath VTE is above the threshold
    When the GUI computes the alarm
    Then the HIGH VTE alarm has medium priority

  Scenario: VTE computation for each breath
    Given multiple breaths with varying VTE values
    When the GUI computes the VTE for each breath
    Then the VTE is computed correctly for each breath

  Scenario: Pressure high alarm cancellation
    Given the pressure high alarm is triggered
    When the alarm is cancelled
    Then the alarm does not re-trigger for 2 minutes

  Scenario: High-priority alarm for O2 input line disconnection
    Given the O2 input line is disconnected
    When the GUI computes the alarm
    Then a high-priority alarm is triggered

  Scenario: Displaying multiple active alarms
    Given multiple alarms are triggered
    When the GUI displays the active alarms
    Then all currently active alarms are displayed

  Scenario: Event log inclusion of confirmed alarm settings
    Given an alarm is confirmed
    When the event log is updated
    Then the confirmed alarm settings are included in the event log

  Scenario Outline: HIGH VTE alarm computation with varying threshold values
    Given the current breath VTE is <vte> above the threshold
    When the GUI computes the alarm
    Then the HIGH VTE alarm is active
    Examples:
      | vte |
      | 1   |
      | 10  |
      | 100 |

  Scenario Outline: LOW VTE alarm priority with varying threshold values
    Given the current breath VTE is <vte> below the threshold
    When the GUI computes the alarm
    Then the LOW VTE alarm has medium priority
    Examples:
      | vte |
      | 1   |
      | 10  |
      | 100 |

  Scenario Outline: HIGH VTE alarm priority with varying threshold values
    Given the current breath VTE is <vte> above the threshold
    When the GUI computes the alarm
    Then the HIGH VTE alarm has medium priority
    Examples:
      | vte |
      | 1   |
      | 10  |
      | 100 |
```
